what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee took no votes on the town manager's redline; its only vote was to adjourn.
Members reached a straw consensus, with no vote, to adopt the town manager's recommendation on who appoints the town accountant, subject to further review.
The committee will research a charter duty for facilities and asset management further, including talking to the School Committee.
The committee agreed to try a staged town survey: a few questions at a time, posted online with paper copies and cutoff dates.
The February 21 meeting is skipped; the committee will meet February 7 and February 28.

why_it_matters: The charter sets who appoints the town accountant and who is chief financial officer, so these drafts shape who controls the town's finances.

A charter duty for maintaining buildings could change how upkeep is funded and supervised. One member said neglect comes from lack of appropriation more than lack of supervisors, and that a position's cost comes out of money for maintenance.
